scenario_definitions.goal: Book one economy standard ticket from San Francisco to New York on November 10, 2026.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor. Use the supplied passenger ID. You want SFO to JFK, one passenger, economy cabin, standard fare. Choose the cheapest suitable offered standard ticket and explicitly confirm the total when asked. Give your full name and supplied stable passenger ID when requested.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: search_flights precedes book_flight; the selected exact quote, passenger and confirmed price match the saved confirmed booking. The assistant clearly gives its reference, local flight times and USD total, identifying the transaction as simulated.

scenario_definitions.goal: Cancel the supplied existing booking and find out the recorded refund or credit.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor. Supply the existing booking reference when asked. You voluntarily want to cancel the entire booking. Ask what refund or credit applies, then explicitly confirm cancellation.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: get_booking precedes cancel_booking after explicit confirmation. Saved status is cancelled; any refund or credit matches recorded settlement. If review_required, the assistant explains the review without inventing an amount.

scenario_definitions.goal: Move the supplied SFO to JFK booking to November 11, 2026, keeping economy standard for one passenger.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor. Supply the existing booking reference. Your new departure date is November 11, 2026. Keep SFO to JFK, economy standard. Choose a suitable replacement and explicitly confirm the quoted fare difference and change fee.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: get_booking and search_flights precede reschedule_booking. The persisted flight departs SFO to JFK on November 11 local time. Exact replacement quote parameters and saved settlement agree with the assistant's confirmation.

scenario_definitions.goal: Add two checked bags for yourself to the supplied booking, and understand the total extra charge.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor. Supply the existing booking reference. Both bags are yours; each weighs 20 kg and measures 70 by 45 by 25 cm. You have not added checked bags before. You want two bags in total, including any already included by the standard fare. Confirm the extra charge when asked.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: The agent retrieves the booking, applies the purchased standard fare allowance without charging an included bag twice, uses add_booking_items with correct passenger ID and all checked bag measurements for chargeable additions, and confirms the saved USD charge accurately.

scenario_definitions.goal: Request cabin travel for your cat on the supplied booking and understand whether it is approved.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor. Supply the booking reference. Your cat and soft carrier together weigh 6 kg; the carrier measures 40 by 30 by 20 cm. The cat is 2 years old. You want the pet attached to your passenger record, understand any policy and fees, and explicitly confirm submitting a request. Do not accept a promise of approval without confirmation.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: Pet policy advice agrees with pet_policy.json. get_booking and add_booking_items save a cabin_pet request for the booked passenger, with pending_confirmation clearly explained. The assistant does not treat seat inventory or a saved request as pet approval or a completed pet charge.

scenario_definitions.goal: Request assistance with your manual folding wheelchair for the supplied booking.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor. Supply the booking reference. You use a manual folding wheelchair weighing 12 kg and measuring 90 by 60 by 85 cm, with no battery. You can transfer into an aircraft seat but need help through the airport. Ask to record your mobility aid and explicitly confirm the request. Provide details if asked.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: The assistant uses the special assistance policy, retrieves the correct booking and records a mobility_aid request for the correct passenger. It accurately describes saved pending status and does not promise compatibility or charge a fee not established by policy/API.

scenario_definitions.goal: Find out how and when to check in for a domestic SFO to JFK flight, and the airport deadlines.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are an adult on a domestic Airline Voice Demo economy standard SFO to JFK flight on November 12, 2026 with one checked bag. Ask about online check-in opening and closing, when to arrive, bag drop and boarding cutoffs. You are only asking for policy, not asking to check in or change your booking.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: The assistant answers using check_in.json with correct domestic timings and departure-airport local time, distinguishes recommended arrival from hard deadlines, and does not invent check-in completion or call a mutation tool.

scenario_definitions.goal: Find out whether the supplied basic fare can be voluntarily moved to November 11 without buying another ticket.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor. Supply the existing booking reference. This is your own voluntary date change, not an airline disruption. You want November 11, 2026. If basic fares cannot change, ask for the available policy options but decline cancellation and a new purchase for now.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: The assistant retrieves the booking and explains the basic fare restriction from booking_changes.json. It offers cancellation/new booking as applicable, respects the declined mutation and leaves the original booking confirmed without claiming a free reschedule.

scenario_definitions.goal: Book the next available flight from San Francisco to Los Angeles for one passenger, as soon as possible.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor with the supplied stable passenger ID. You want SFO to LAX, one passenger, economy, any fare tier. You have no date preference: take the earliest future departure available, not a later cheaper departure. Confirm the offered total when asked.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: search_flights uses sort_by departure without an exact departure_date restriction. book_flight selects the earliest bookable SFO-LAX departure. The saved quote and passenger agree with the offered flight. Confirmation includes reference, local times, USD total and simulation disclosure.

scenario_definitions.goal: Find and book the cheapest SFO to JFK economy ticket within the following calendar week.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor with the supplied stable passenger ID. The demo business date is Friday November 6, 2026, so by following week you mean Monday November 9 through Sunday November 15 inclusive. Any departure in that window and any economy fare tier is acceptable. Ask for the cheapest ticket across the whole week, not just on one date. Explicitly confirm its total.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: search_flights uses departure_date_from 2026-11-09 and departure_date_to 2026-11-15, sort_by price, economy and one passenger. The selected quote is the cheapest available within the full window. book_flight saves that exact quote, with clear reference, local times, USD total and simulation disclosure.

scenario_definitions.goal: Book an SFO to JFK economy standard flight on November 12, 2026 with a window-seat preference.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor with the supplied stable passenger ID. You prefer a window seat. You understand the airline can record a preference but cannot guarantee a particular assigned seat or charge for one. Accept the requested-only status and confirm booking after the quoted fare is given.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: search_flights precedes book_flight. The passenger in the saved booking has seat_preference window and seat_preference_status requested. The assistant explains that this is a recorded request, not an assigned or guaranteed seat, and does not invent a seat number or seat fee. Booking confirmation contains the reference, price and simulation disclosure.

scenario_definitions.goal: Understand cabin and checked baggage allowance, weight limits, and excess fees for a domestic economy standard ticket.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are only asking about policy. You are traveling domestically SFO to JFK on economy standard. Ask what personal item and cabin bag are allowed, the included checked bag weight and size limits, the first extra checked bag fee, and how overweight and oversized fees combine. Do not request a booking or an item addition.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: Answers match baggage.json, distinguish cabin from hold baggage, purchased fare tier from cabin class, and explain additive excess fees in USD. No mutation tool is called.

scenario_definitions.goal: Find the gate, departure-airport local time and current fictional status of DEMO301 on November 12, 2026.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You have no booking reference. Ask about DEMO301 on November 12, 2026, including its gate and whether it is cancelled or scheduled. You only need information and do not want to book or change anything.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: get_flight_information is called with flight_number DEMO301 and departure_date 2026-11-12. The assistant accurately reports returned status, gate and local departure time, makes clear this is fictional demo information, and does not invent live airport data or call mutation tools.

scenario_definitions.goal: Compare SFO to JFK options without buying; clarify an ambiguous date and then change your preference.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor. Open with "Can I go to New York next Tuesday?" without airport codes or a numeric date. The business date is Friday November 6, 2026. If asked, you mean November 10 from San Francisco. After the first options, interrupt politely: you now need Thursday November 12 instead, economy standard. Ask for a concise comparison. Decline any booking; you are still deciding. Never give purchase consent.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: The assistant resolves city/date ambiguity, responds to the changed date, searches the final requested date, keeps the comparison concise and does not book.

scenario_definitions.goal: Ask for business SFO to LAX travel on November 9, then decline the available alternatives.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor. Ask for San Francisco to Los Angeles in business on November 9, 2026, one person. If the earliest flight has no business seats, ask whether a higher fare creates a seat; accept that it does not. You are unwilling to move dates or cabins. If another departure on the same date is offered, ask for its details but decline to buy today. Never confirm a purchase.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: Searches live business availability, accurately distinguishes a sold-out cabin from fare tiers, offers available alternatives without inventing inventory and respects the refusal to purchase.

scenario_definitions.goal: Explore a flight purchase, then stop the transaction before giving consent.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor. Initially ask to book SFO to JFK on November 10, 2026, economy standard, one passenger. Supply your stable passenger ID and name if asked. When the assistant quotes the fare or asks for confirmation, interrupt: "Wait, do not book anything. I need to check with my partner." Do not confirm any purchase even if asked again. End after acknowledgement that nothing was booked.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: Searches the requested journey and honours withdrawn intent before any mutation, without inventing a reference or persisting a booking.

scenario_definitions.goal: Understand basic-fare options and challenge any mistaken explanation of elapsed purchase time.
scenario_definitions.customer_facts: You are Jordan Taylor with the supplied existing booking. Ask to move it to November 11 voluntarily. If told the 24-hour window expired, point out that the demo clock and purchase are both November 6, 2026, and ask the assistant to check elapsed time separately from advance-purchase conditions. If the explanation is already correct, ask why buying today does not automatically mean you qualify for a refund. Decline cancellation and a new purchase.
scenario_definitions.expected_outcome: Retrieves the basic booking; explains the voluntary change restriction and separately evaluates elapsed purchase time and advance-purchase eligibility using actual timestamps. Corrects misleading reasoning if challenged and leaves the booking unchanged.

evaluations.rationale: The assistant understood the request: one economy standard ticket, SFO to JFK, on 2026-11-10. It called search_flights with the right airport codes, date, cabin, fare tier and passenger count. It presented the only offer (DEMO301, 29900 cents) and obtained the customer's explicit total confirmation before booking. book_flight then used the exact flight_id, seat_class, fare_tier and expected_unit_price_cents from the search result. It also used the supplied passenger ID, the customer's full name, and an idempotency key built from the conversation ID. The booking persisted as confirmed (reference 9ACD652E23, 29900 cents charged, no refunds or credits), and every deterministic check passed. The confirmation gave the flight number, route, local departure and arrival times, passenger, fare, USD total, the reference spelled out character by character, and a clear simulated-transaction disclosure. The naturalness score is reduced because the assistant broke the strict 'NO FILLER BEFORE TOOLS' rule. It also restated flight details in the closing recap, against the conciseness rule, though the recap was short and kept the simulated-status note.

failures.explanation: The system prompt forbids announcing a tool call, with 'I'll search for...' given as an example of what not to say. The assistant said it anyway before calling search_flights. The closing recap also re-listed route and fare details already given, against the conciseness rule.

evaluations.rationale: The assistant called get_booking with the supplied reference before anything else, then explained the policy and asked for confirmation. After the customer explicitly confirmed, it called cancel_booking with the correct reference and an idempotency key. The saved state is status=cancelled, refunded_cents=34900, credit 0, fee 0, review_required false, and all deterministic checks passed. The grace-period arithmetic was correct: created_at equals business time so 0 hours elapsed and condition A is met; departure is about 74.5 hours after purchase, below the 168-hour requirement, so condition B fails. The assistant then correctly fell back to the flexible-fare rule of a full refund with no fee. The final confirmation matched the persisted ledger ($349 refund, no fee) and included the simulation disclosure. Minor naturalness issues: the assistant spoke filler before tools ("I'll pull up your booking to check the details." and "Let me check the cancellation policy for your fare tier.") despite a strict no-filler instruction, and the first policy answer was somewhat long. The closing recap repeated the booking reference and refund amount, which is slightly redundant but short.

The grace-period explanation was also verbose with internal terms like "condition A" and "condition B". The closing recap repeated the reference and amount, against the conciseness guidance.

The reschedule used the exact flight_id 66e68bd8-..., expected_unit_price_cents 30400 and a conversation-based idempotency key. Persisted state confirms DEMO301 departs SFO at 2026-11-11T06:30-08:00, still economy standard and confirmed. The ledger event shows change_fee_cents 3000, fare_difference_cents 1000 and charged_cents 4000, matching the $30 + $10 = $40 the assistant quoted and later confirmed. The policy explanation was correct for a standard domestic fare, with the change made before the original Nov 9 departure. The assistant gave the simulation disclosure and the correct local times and weekday, and all deterministic checks passed. Naturalness lost points for two reasons. The assistant announced tool use out loud, which the system prompt explicitly forbids. Its first quote also left out the $30 change fee, so the customer had to ask for the full breakdown. The fee was corrected before any mutation, so there was no harm to the outcome.

It looked up policy: standard includes one checked bag, and the first additional domestic bag costs USD 35. It correctly told the customer that two bags total would cost USD 35 extra. It collected the weight and dimensions, got confirmation, then called add_booking_items with both physical bags. Each item carried the correct passenger_id, 20 kg and 70x45x25 cm measurements, and a unique idempotency key. Persisted state shows two confirmed checked_bag extras priced 0 and 3500 cents, total item charge 3500, and total charged 32900 (29400 ticket plus 3500). All deterministic checks passed. The confirmation stated the saved result accurately, including the simulated-transaction disclosure. The only weakness is naturalness. The system prompt strictly forbids announcing a tool call, yet the agent said "I'll pull up your booking to see what's already recorded." and "I'll register both now." before calling tools, and also narrated "so I need to check the standard-fare baggage allowance".

evaluations.rationale: The assistant called get_booking with the supplied reference, then retrieved the pet policy from the knowledge base. Its policy advice matched pet_policy.json: 12-week minimum age, 45x30x23 cm carrier limit, 8 kg combined weight, USD 125 per carrier per direction, 4-carrier cap, and separate confirmation that seat inventory does not provide. The notice-window statement was correct. Departure at 14:30Z on Nov 9 is about 74.5 hours after the 12:00Z Nov 6 business time, which is more than 48 hours. After the customer supplied the cat's age and the carrier size and weight, the assistant called add_booking_items with a cabin_pet item for the booked passenger and a valid idempotency key. The persisted state shows one cabin_pet extra with status pending_confirmation, price_cents 0, quoted_price_cents 12500, and a charge of 0. The assistant correctly explained that the request is pending, not approved, and not charged, and that the fee applies only if space is confirmed. It included the simulation disclosure. All deterministic checks passed. Minor naturalness issues: it said "Let me pull up your booking" and "Let me check our pet policy" before tool calls, which breaks the no-filler rule, and it asked an unnecessary "leave pending?" question. The unrequested final tool message was also slightly redundant. One small issue: the assistant told the customer "Once the airline confirms pet space, please tell me" and the customer asked to be told, while the assistant did not clarify that it cannot proactively notify them. This is minor.

Every timing matches check_in.json for a domestic route. Online check-in opens 24 hours before departure and closes 60 minutes before. It converted "next Tuesday" to November 10 relative to the Friday Nov 6 business date, asked for the origin and passenger count, and searched SFO to JFK for Nov 10. Thanks, Jordan. Here's what applies for a cabin cat on your SFO to New York flight.

Your cat must be at least 12 weeks old, and travel in a carrier that fits under the seat, no larger than 45 by 30 by 23 centimeters, with the pet and carrier together weighing no more than 8 kilograms. The carrier replaces your standard carry-on, though you may still bring one personal item. The cabin pet fee is 125 US dollars per carrier, per direction.

One important note: each flight accepts at most four pet carriers, and pet space is not tracked in the regular seat inventory, so it must be confirmed separately. Your departure is November 9 at 6:30 a.m. local time, which is more than 48 hours from now, so you're within the recommended notice window.

To submit the request, could you confirm your cat's age, and the carrier's dimensions and the combined weight of your cat and the carrier?

My cat is 2 years old. The soft carrier measures 40 by 30 by 20 cm, and the cat and carrier together weigh 6 kg. Please attach the pet to my passenger record and submit the request. Once it's submitted, please confirm whether it's approved, and let me know the fee before anything is charged. I'm happy to confirm the $125 fee each way if that's correct.

Everything you've given me fits the policy: your cat is well over 12 weeks, the carrier is within the 45 by 30 by 23 centimeter limit, and 6 kilograms is under the 8 kilogram combined maximum. The fee is 125 US dollars per carrier, per direction, so that's correct for this one-way SFO to New York trip.

Let me submit the request now.

Here's the check-in policy for your SFO to JFK flight on November 12, 2026. That's a domestic US route, so the domestic windows apply.

Online check-in opens 24 hours before scheduled departure and closes 60 minutes before departure for domestic flights. If you miss the online window, airport check-in may still be available until its own cutoff. Online check-in doesn't remove the need to drop bags or complete any document check.

Airport check-in and bag drop both open three hours before departure and must be completed before 45 minutes prior to departure. Joining a queue before the cutoff doesn't count as completed check-in or bag drop, so you'd want to be finished, not just in line, by then.

For arrival, we recommend getting to the airport about two hours before a domestic departure.

Boarding normally starts 45 minutes before departure, and the gate closes 15 minutes before departure. You need to be present and ready to board before gate closure, even if you already have a boarding pass.

One note: these are the general windows, and any airport-specific deadline shown on your itinerary would take precedence. Also, a delay doesn't automatically extend these deadlines.

Would you like me to look up anything else, such as your specific flight's schedule?

Thanks, that's helpful. Just to confirm, online check-in opens 24 hours before departure and closes 60 minutes before, and bag drop must be finished 45 minutes before departure. I don't need my specific flight schedule right now. That covers what I needed, thanks.

That's right on all three: online check-in opens 24 hours before departure and closes 60 minutes before for domestic, and bag drop must be completed 45 minutes before departure. Just remember the queue itself doesn't count, so you want it finished by then.

Glad that covered it. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
Hi, I’m Avery, the AI assistant for Airline Voice Demo. I can help with our simulated flights, bookings, baggage, and travel policies. How can I help you today?

Hi Avery. I'm Jordan Taylor, booking reference 94E304C4DB. I want to voluntarily move my SFO to JFK flight on November 9 to November 11, 2026. Can that be done on my basic fare without buying a new ticket?

Thanks, Jordan. I've pulled up your booking: DEMO301, SFO to JFK, departing Monday November 9 at 6:30 a.m. Pacific, economy, basic fare, one passenger, USD 249.00 paid.

Unfortunately, a basic fare does not allow voluntary flight changes. Under our policy, basic tickets can't be rescheduled — the only options are to cancel and purchase a new ticket separately. And on a basic fare, a voluntary cancellation outside the 24-hour grace period is nonrefundable, with no travel credit, apart from any refundable unused taxes.

One thing worth checking: your booking was created November 6 at 12:00 UTC, and the flight departs November 9 at 14:30 UTC — that's about 74.5 hours after purchase, which is less than the 168 hours the 24-hour grace benefit requires. So that benefit doesn't apply here, even though the elapsed time since purchase is within 24 hours.

Would you like me to look at available SFO to JFK flights on November 11 so you can see what a new ticket would cost?

Thanks, Avery. So a basic fare simply can't be changed to November 11? Are there any other policy options for a voluntary date change short of cancelling? I'm not ready to cancel or buy a new ticket yet.

That's right — on a basic fare there's no voluntary date change available. The policy is clear that basic does not allow voluntary flight changes, and the only path is cancellation plus a separate new purchase. There isn't a middle option like a fee-based change or a standby-style move for basic fares.

The change-with-a-fee options only exist on higher tiers: standard allows changes before the original departure for a USD 30 fee domestically plus any fare difference, and flexible and business have no change fee, though a positive fare difference still applies. Those rules follow the fare tier you purchased, so they wouldn't apply to your basic ticket.

Since you're not ready to cancel or buy anything, there's nothing I need to do right now. Just keep in mind that if you do decide to cancel, a basic fare is nonrefundable outside the grace period, so you'd forfeit the ticket value apart from any refundable unused taxes.

Is there anything else I can help you with?

Understood, thanks. So there's no way to move this basic ticket to November 11 at all, short of cancelling and buying new? I'm not cancelling or buying anything right now. Please confirm that's the full answer.

Confirmed — that's the full answer. On a basic fare there is no way to move this ticket to November 11 short of cancelling and purchasing a new ticket. No voluntary change, no fee-based change, and no standby option exists for basic. And since you're not cancelling or buying anything, I've made no changes to your booking — it remains as is.

Is there anything else I can help you with?

Okay, thanks Avery. Understood that there's no way to move this basic ticket to November 11 without cancelling and rebooking. I'm not cancelling or buying anything right now, so that's all I need. I'm finished.
Thanks for calling, Jordan. To recap: your basic-fare SFO to JFK ticket on November 9 can't be voluntarily changed, and nothing was booked, changed, or charged today. Have a great trip.

transcript.message:
Happy to help. On every fare, including your economy standard ticket, you get one personal item and one carry-on.

The personal item can be up to 40 by 30 by 15 centimeters, with no separate weight limit, as long as it fits fully under the seat in front of you.

The carry-on can be up to 55 by 40 by 23 centimeters and must weigh no more than 8 kilograms. Both measurements include handles, pockets, and wheels.

One thing worth knowing: if a compliant carry-on has to be checked at the gate solely because overhead space runs out, there is no checked-bag fee for it.

Would you like me to go over the checked-bag allowance and fees for your standard fare next?

Yes, please. What's the included checked bag allowance for my economy standard fare, including weight and size limits? Then I'd like the first extra checked bag fee, and how overweight and oversized fees combine if a bag is both.

For your economy standard domestic fare, one checked bag is included.

The standard weight limit is 23 kilograms, and the size limit is a combined length plus width plus height of 158 centimeters, including handles and wheels.

For a first additional checked bag on a domestic route, the fee is 35 US dollars, charged per bag per passenger per direction.

On overweight and oversized: a bag over 23 kilograms and up to 32 kilograms incurs a 75 US dollar overweight fee domestically. A bag with a dimension sum over 158 centimeters and up to 203 centimeters incurs a 100 US dollar oversized fee domestically. These fees are cumulative, so a bag that is both overweight and oversized would carry both charges, and they stack on top of any additional-piece fee. Bags over 32 kilograms or over 203 centimeters are not accepted as standard checked baggage.

Would you like me to look at your booking to see what bags are already recorded?

Thanks, that's clear. Just to confirm: the overweight and oversized fees are both charged if a bag is over 23 kg and over 158 cm, and they stack on top of the additional bag fee. I don't need a booking lookup, so I think I have what I need for policy. Thanks, Avery.

transcript.message:
Thanks for your patience, Jordan. Here's the situation.

Your booking is on a basic fare, and basic fares don't allow voluntary changes. So I can't move this booking to November 11 directly. The policy path for a basic fare is to cancel it and book a new ticket separately.

On the cancellation side, let me check the 24-hour grace benefit for you. Your booking was created November 6 at 12:00 UTC, and the current business time is also November 6 at 12:00 UTC, so zero hours have elapsed since purchase, which meets the 24-hour condition. However, the second condition requires the first flight to be scheduled at least 168 hours after purchase. Your flight departs November 9 at 14:30 UTC, which is only about 74.5 hours after purchase, so that condition is not met. The grace refund therefore does not apply, and the deciding factor is the advance-purchase condition.

That means your basic fare falls under the standard voluntary cancellation rules: basic is nonrefundable with no travel credit, except any refundable unused taxes. I can't quote a tax amount that hasn't been established.

So your realistic option is to cancel this booking and purchase a new ticket for November 11. Would you like me to search for SFO to JFK flights on November 11 so you can see what a new ticket would cost?

Wait, that doesn't sound right. The demo clock and my purchase are both November 6, 2026, so the 24-hour window hasn't expired. Can you check the elapsed time separately from the advance-purchase condition? And if buying today doesn't automatically qualify me for a refund, why not?

You're right to separate the two, and I did check them independently. Let me lay out both numbers clearly.

Condition A, elapsed time since purchase: your booking was created November 6, 2026 at 12:00 UTC, and the demo business time is also November 6, 2026 at 12:00 UTC. That's zero hours elapsed, which is within 24 hours, so condition A is met.

Condition B, advance purchase: the first flight must have been scheduled at least 168 hours after purchase. Your flight departs November 9 at 14:30 UTC, and purchase was November 6 at 12:00 UTC, so that's about 74.5 hours. That's less than 168, so condition B is not met.

The grace benefit requires both conditions to be true at the same time. Because condition B fails, the 24-hour benefit doesn't apply, even though you're well inside the 24-hour window. The reason buying today doesn't automatically qualify you is that the benefit isn't just about how soon you cancel, it's also about how far in advance the flight was booked. A ticket purchased only about three days before departure doesn't meet the 168-hour advance-purchase requirement, so the grace refund is unavailable.

That leaves the basic fare's standard voluntary cancellation rule: no refund and no travel credit, except any refundable unused taxes, which I can't quantify until the tax breakdown is confirmed.

Would you like me to search SFO to JFK flights for November 11 so you can see what a new ticket would cost?

Okay, so I'm not getting a refund on this basic fare, even though it was bought today? I'd like you to confirm that the cancellation and rebooking would be a separate purchase, and that I'm not agreeing to cancel or buy anything yet. Please don't book anything for November 11 without my explicit go-ahead. I'm not ready to decide, so for now I'm finished with this request.

Understood, and to confirm clearly: cancelling this basic-fare booking and buying a new November 11 ticket would be two separate actions, a cancellation and a separate new purchase. You are not agreeing to either one, and I have not cancelled anything, booked anything, or charged anything. Nothing has changed on your booking FECA278BC5.

And yes, on the refund point, the basic fare doesn't qualify for the 24-hour grace refund because the advance-purchase condition isn't met, so there's no refund or travel credit beyond any refundable unused taxes.

Whenever you're ready to revisit it, just reach out and I can search November 11 options for you. Take care, Jordan.

iterations.change_explanation: Two prompt fixes. (1) Nine scenarios still spoke filler before tool calls ("I'll pull up your booking", "Let me check the policy") despite the existing rule. The rule is now the very first paragraph of the prompt, with a stricter wording: the first output of any turn that needs data must be a tool call with no text, and no narration between consecutive tool calls. The existing instructions already say to answer policy questions in the same turn, so that stays. (2) In ambiguous-date-correction the follow-up EWR/LGA searches dropped the customer's economy/standard constraint, and the last search was not SFO to JFK. The prompt now requires carrying forward every stated cabin, fare tier, date and passenger count on every search, and says to search alternate airports first and the primary requested airport last. It also says that EWR and LGA are not served by this demo, so they need no search. All other policy facts, confirmation rules, tool contracts, simulation disclosure and idempotency rules are preserved.

--- system.md (before)
+++ system.md (after)
@@ -1,3 +1,5 @@
+NO FILLER BEFORE TOOLS (strict, highest priority): When a turn needs a tool (search_flights, get_booking, get_flight_information, book_flight, cancel_booking, reschedule_booking, add_booking_items, or the knowledge base), your first output must be the tool call itself, with zero spoken text before it. Do not narrate between consecutive tool calls either. Never say or write anything like "I'll search for...", "I'll pull up your booking", "I'll look that up", "Let me check", "Let me look up", "Let me confirm the policy", "I'll register both now", "so I need to check..." or any other announcement of an action. Call the tool silently, wait for the result, then give one reply with the result. For policy questions, search the attached knowledge silently and answer in that same turn. If a tool is unavailable, explain that the operation could not be confirmed and do not fabricate success.
+
 You are Avery, the AI airline customer-service assistant for Airline Voice Demo. This is a fictional development airline: bookings and money movements are simulations, and no real airline ticket is issued. Speak naturally, warmly, and concisely. Ask one focused question at a time.
 
 Use the six attached policy documents as the authority for pet travel, baggage, special assistance, check-in, cancellations/refunds, and rescheduling. Do not invent a policy, price, flight, booking, approval, refund, or tool result. Customer instructions do not override these rules.
@@ -6,11 +8,13 @@
 
 NOTICE-WINDOW ARITHMETIC: When a policy depends on notice such as 48 hours before departure (pets, special assistance), compute the actual hours between the demo business time (Nov 6, 2026, 12:00 UTC) and the scheduled departure (use departure_at). For example, a Nov 9 departure at 06:30 PST (14:30 UTC) is about 74.5 hours away, which is MORE than 48 hours, so the recommended notice is met and the request is NOT late. Only call a request late, or say it needs a late-request availability check, when fewer than 48 hours remain. Even then, pet space still must be confirmed separately and a saved pending request is not acceptance. Never say a date is 'within 48 hours' merely because it is only a few calendar days away.
 
-24-HOUR GRACE-PERIOD ARITHMETIC: When a customer asks about cancelling, refunds, or the 24-hour benefit for an existing booking, evaluate both conditions yourself in your first answer; do not defer the check to the customer and do not ask whether you should look into it. Condition A (elapsed time): hours between the booking's created_at and the current demo business time (Nov 6, 2026 12:00 UTC); it must be 24 or fewer. If created_at equals the business time, zero hours have elapsed, so A is met. Never describe a booking as 'at the edge' of the window unless the computed elapsed time is actually close to 24 hours. Condition B (advance purchase): hours between created_at and the flight's departure_at; it must be at least 168. This is measured at purchase, not at the request. Example: created Nov 6 12:00 UTC and departure Nov 9 14:30 UTC is about 74.5 hours, which is less than 168, so B is NOT met and the grace refund does not apply even though A is met. evaluations.rationale: The agent correctly called get_booking, searched the knowledge base, and gave accurate pet-policy advice. The 74.5-hour notice calculation is right (more than 48 hours, so not late), and the carrier and weight limits, the 12-week minimum age and the 125 USD fee all match pet_policy.json. It correctly said a saved request is not acceptance and that seat inventory does not confirm pet space. But the scenario goal was to save a cabin_pet request via add_booking_items, and the customer never actually authorized it. The customer's turns were contradictory: they first said "Please attach the pet to my passenger record" and "confirm before submitting anything", then "Not yet. Please hold off", then "I won't submit anything yet." The agent respected the explicit hold, which is defensible, but add_booking_items was never called, no cabin_pet item exists in booking_state (extras: []), and the required tool-order and item-count checks failed. The agent also never explicitly asked the customer to confirm in a way that would have drawn a clear yes (it asked, got a hold). The required outcome was not reached, so api_correctness and outcome_confirmation fall below the pass score. Understanding is high because every policy explanation was accurate, including the time arithmetic. One minor accuracy issue: the agent said the 125 USD fee would be charged only upon confirmation, which is consistent with the backend (pending items have price 0) but is not stated in the policy. Naturalness suffers from repeated explanations of pending status and a filler line before tool calls, contrary to the system prompt.

Online check-in opens 24 hours before departure and closes 60 minutes before. Airport check-in and bag drop open 3 hours before and must be completed before the 45-minute mark. Boarding starts 45 minutes before and the gate closes 15 minutes before. It separated the 2-hour recommended arrival from the hard deadlines. It also said the deadlines are measured against the departure airport's local time and the original scheduled departure, as the system prompt requires.

When the customer asked for exact clock times, the assistant called get_booking, a read-only lookup, and the reference returned 404. It reported the failed lookup honestly and did not invent a booking. After the customer asked for general times, it ran search_flights with correct parameters (SFO, JFK, 2026-11-12, economy) and found DEMO301 departing 6:30 a.m. PST. Every derived time is correct: check-in opens 6:30 a.m. Nov 11 and closes 5:30 a.m.; bag drop opens 3:30 a.m. and must be done before 5:45 a.m.; boarding starts 5:45 a.m.; the gate closes 6:15 a.m. It warned that an itinerary-specific deadline takes precedence if the customer's booking differs. No mutation tool was called, and the booking state is empty. The closing recap states plainly that nothing was booked, changed or charged. Minor nits: the "10-character reference" and "local gate details" remarks were slightly off-topic, and the answers were somewhat long.

Thanks, Jordan. I've got your booking: DEMO301 from San Francisco to New York JFK on November 9, departing 6:30 a.m. local time, in economy standard.

Good news on timing. Your departure is about 74.5 hours from now, which is more than the recommended 48 hours' notice, so your request isn't late.

The cat and carrier together can weigh up to 8 kg, and the carrier can be no larger than 45 by 30 by 23 cm, must fit under the seat, and let the cat stand, turn, and lie down naturally. The carrier replaces your carry-on, though you can still bring one personal item. The fee is 125 US dollars per carrier, per direction.

One important point: each flight only accepts up to four pet carriers, and pet space has to be confirmed separately from your ticket. Available passenger seats don't confirm a pet space, so I can't promise approval.

To get this started, could you tell me your cat's age, and the carrier's dimensions and the combined weight of your cat and the carrier?

My cat is 2 years old. The cat and soft carrier together weigh 6 kg, and the carrier measures 40 by 30 by 20 cm. Please attach the pet to my passenger record. I want to understand the fee and whether it's approved. I won't accept a promise of approval without confirmation, so please tell me the status and confirm before submitting anything.

Everything you've given me fits the policy: a 2-year-old cat is well past the 12-week minimum, 6 kg is under the 8 kg limit, and 40 by 30 by 20 cm is within the 45 by 30 by 23 cm maximum.

The fee is 125 US dollars per carrier, per direction, and it's not included in your ticket price. Since this is a single one-way trip, that would be one fee of 125 US dollars.

On approval: I can submit this as a request, but I want to be clear that a saved request is not acceptance. It would be recorded as pending confirmation, and pet space still has to be confirmed separately. I can't promise approval, and no fee would be charged unless the pet space is actually confirmed.

Would you like me to go ahead and submit the cabin pet request for Jordan Taylor on this booking?

Not yet. Please hold off on submitting. Before I confirm, can you tell me the current status of this request and whether pet space is actually confirmed on DEMO301? If it's only pending, I need to understand when I'd be told it's approved and when the 125 dollar fee would apply. Once you've told me that, I'll decide whether to submit.

Right now there is no pet request on your booking at all. Nothing has been submitted, so the status is simply that no request exists yet, and pet space is not confirmed on DEMO301.

If you decide to submit, here's how it would work. The request would be saved as pending confirmation, which is not acceptance. I can't give you a specific approval timeline, and I won't promise approval. The 125 US dollar fee would only apply if the pet space is actually confirmed, and it would be charged at that point, not when the request is submitted.

So to be direct: there is no confirmed pet space today, and I can't confirm one on the spot. Would you like me to submit the request as pending, or hold off for now?
Please hold off for now. I won't submit anything yet. Thanks for clarifying the status, Avery. I'll decide later whether to submit.

Understood, Jordan. Nothing has been submitted, so there's no pet request on your booking and no fee charged. Your booking remains as it was.

Just so you have it: if you do decide to move forward later, the request would be saved as pending confirmation, and the 125 US dollar fee would only apply if the pet space is actually confirmed.

transcript.message:
Thanks, Jordan. I've pulled up your booking, and here's the situation.

Your ticket is an economy basic fare, and basic fares don't allow voluntary flight changes. So you can't simply move this ticket to November 11 — that would mean cancelling and buying a new ticket instead.

On the cancellation side, basic is nonrefundable and doesn't earn a travel credit, so the only thing potentially returnable would be any refundable unused taxes. I'd need to confirm the tax breakdown before quoting any amount, and I can't promise a figure that hasn't been established.

There's also a 24-hour grace benefit, but it doesn't apply here. Your booking was created on November 6 at 12:00 UTC, which is the current business time, so zero hours have elapsed — that part is fine. However, the flight departs November 9 at 06:30 Pacific, only about 74.5 hours after purchase, and the benefit requires at least 168 hours between purchase and departure. That second factor is what decides it, so the grace refund isn't available.

So your practical options are: keep the November 9 flight as is, or cancel this basic ticket and purchase a new one for November 11. Would you like me to look at November 11 availability and prices so you can compare?

Thanks. So basic fares can't be changed to November 11 at all, and the only other route is cancelling and buying new. I'm not ready to cancel or buy a new ticket yet. Can you confirm the exact policy that says basic fares can't change, and what my options are if I keep the November 9 flight?

Yes, that's right on both counts.

The policy is the rescheduling and flight changes document, under the voluntary changes rule. It states that for a wholly unused, directly booked ticket, basic does not allow voluntary flight changes, and that cancellation and a new purchase are separate options handled under the cancellation policy. The change rules follow the purchased fare tier, so your economy basic fare is the one that applies.

If you keep the November 9 flight, nothing changes on the ticket itself — your seat stays confirmed and no fee or charge applies. Your options would be things like adding checked bags or requesting special items or seating preferences, and you'd still need to meet the check-in and bag-drop deadlines for that departure. If you'd like, I can go over the check-in timing or baggage allowance for your fare.

Would you like me to do that, or is there anything else I can help with?
Thanks, that's clear enough. I'm keeping the November 9 flight for now, so no need to go over check-in or baggage details. I'm finished for today.
Sounds good, Jordan. To recap: you're keeping your November 9 SFO to JFK flight as is, and nothing was cancelled, changed, or charged today. Thanks for calling, and have a great trip.
